name: Mt. Lemmon / Catalina Highway
description: Twenty-seven miles of sweepers and switchbacks climbing from saguaro desert to pine forest. Windy Point is the payoff. Gas up in Tucson — there is no fuel on the mountain.
bestSeason: Year-round; cool escape in summer, watch ice Dec-Feb

from.name: Catalina Hwy at Tanque Verde, Tucson AZ

name: Coronado Trail (US-191)
description: Legendary 120-mile ribbon with over 400 curves between Clifton and Alpine. No services for long stretches, no cell coverage, and elk on the road at dusk. One of the best motorcycle roads in America.
bestSeason: May-October; upper sections close with snow

name: Salt River Canyon (US-60)
description: Globe to Show Low through a mile-deep canyon. Long sweeping descents, a bridge at the bottom, then a hard climb back out. Heavy truck traffic — pick your passes carefully.

name: Apache Trail to Tortilla Flat (SR-88)
description: Tight paved twisties along Canyon Lake out to Tortilla Flat. The dirt section past Tortilla Flat has been closed by washouts — turn around there unless you are on an adventure bike and have checked ADOT.

name: Oak Creek Canyon (SR-89A)
description: Red rock into pine over 28 miles, finishing with the famous switchbacks up the canyon wall. Gorgeous and slow — expect tourist traffic on weekends. Ride it early.

name: Kingman to Oatman on Route 66
description: The original Route 66 over Sitgreaves Pass. Gold Hill Grade is a series of blind, unguarded hairpins — genuinely technical. Wild burros wander the street in Oatman, so keep it slow in town.

name: Las Vegas to Valley of Fire
description: Escape from Vegas into red sandstone. The park road itself is smooth, empty, and stunning. Carry water — there is nothing out there and summer temps top 110F.

to.name: Valley of Fire Visitor Center, NV

name: Zion Mt. Carmel Highway (SR-9)
description: Springdale up the switchbacks, through the 1930 tunnel, out to Mt. Carmel Junction. Motorcycles pay the park fee and ride through the tunnel normally — no escort needed. Book ends of the day are best.

name: Gila Cliff Dwellings (NM-15)
description: Forty-four miles that take two hours on purpose. NM-15 is barely two lanes wide with endless blind corners through the Gila. No fuel past Pinos Altos. Best pure motorcycle road in New Mexico.

name: Mt. Graham Swift Trail (SR-366)
description: Climbs 6,000 feet in about 20 miles with more than 100 curves. Pavement ends near the top. Upper gate closes mid-November to mid-April. Cool air and almost no traffic.

to.name: Mt. Graham Swift Trail summit area, AZ

name: Willcox to Chiricahua National Monument
description: Grassland run out to the Wonderland of Rocks, then the eight-mile Bonita Canyon Drive up to Massai Point. Quiet, high, and full of hoodoos. Fuel in Willcox — nothing at the monument.

name: Tucson to Bisbee via SR-80
description: A proper day trip: high desert down to Tombstone, then the climb over Mule Pass into Bisbee's old mining switchbacks. Park at the top of Brewery Gulch and walk. Border Patrol checkpoints on the return.
